Container.Name: OpenWA
Container.Overview:
OpenWA is a free, open-source WhatsApp API Gateway: a REST API plus a bundled React dashboard for running one or more WhatsApp sessions, sending and receiving messages and media, and fanning events out to webhooks.
This template runs the single-container configuration: SQLite database, local media storage, no Redis. Everything persistent (session auth, databases, media, plugins) lives in the single /app/data mapping, so back that folder up and you can rebuild the container freely.
FIRST BOOT: no API key is configured by default, so OpenWA generates a random admin key and writes it into the data folder. Retrieve it with: cat /mnt/user/appdata/openwa/.api-key Then open the WebUI and sign in with that key.
IMPORTANT - READ BEFORE LINKING A NUMBER: OpenWA talks to WhatsApp through reverse-engineered clients (whatsapp-web.js / Baileys), NOT Meta's official Cloud API. There is always a non-zero risk of the account being restricted or banned. Use a dedicated number you can afford to lose, never your primary personal or business number. Not suitable for regulated or compliance-bound deployments.
NO PUID / PGID: unlike most Unraid containers, OpenWA has no PUID/PGID/UMASK support. The image starts as root only long enough to chown /app/data, then drops to a fixed internal user via gosu. Files in the appdata folder therefore end up owned by that image-assigned system UID rather than nobody:users (99:100), and that is normal - do not run Docker Safe New Permissions against it.
MEMORY: the default whatsapp-web.js engine runs a full headless Chromium per session at roughly 300-500 MB each. The 2 GB limit in Extra Parameters comfortably fits 3-4 sessions; raise it for more, or switch ENGINE_TYPE to baileys (30-80 MB per session, but a higher ban-risk profile).

Config.Name: WebUI
Config.Description: REST API and the bundled dashboard share this one port. Swagger, when enabled, is at /api/docs.

Config.Name: Appdata
Config.Description: Holds EVERYTHING persistent: WhatsApp session auth, the SQLite databases, media, installed plugins and the generated first-boot API key (.api-key). Losing this loses your linked sessions and API keys. Keep it on the cache pool - SQLite and the Chromium session profiles do constant small writes that are painfully slow on the array. The container chowns this folder to its own internal user on every start; that is expected, and you should not run Docker Safe New Permissions against it.

Config.Name: Plain-HTTP dashboard fix
Config.Description: LEAVE AS false when reaching the dashboard over plain http on your LAN. With it true (the production default) the browser upgrades the dashboard's own scripts to https, the non-TLS server cannot answer, and you get a BLANK WHITE PAGE. Set it true only once OpenWA sits behind a TLS-terminating reverse proxy such as SWAG or Nginx Proxy Manager.

Config.Name: Auto-start sessions on boot
Config.Description: Re-connect previously authenticated WhatsApp sessions when the container starts. Without this, sessions sit at disconnected after an Unraid reboot or a container update until you start them by hand in the dashboard.

Config.Name: WhatsApp engine
Config.Description: whatsapp-web.js drives a real headless Chromium - lower ban risk, ~300-500 MB RAM per session. baileys speaks the multi-device protocol directly - ~30-80 MB per session, but easier for WhatsApp to fingerprint and therefore a higher ban risk. Prefer whatsapp-web.js unless you need session density.

Config.Name: Master API key
Config.Description: OPTIONAL. Leave EMPTY and OpenWA generates a random admin key on first boot, written to /mnt/user/appdata/openwa/.api-key - read it from there to sign in. If you do set one it must be at least 32 characters and not a known placeholder, or the container refuses to start in production mode. Generate one with: openssl rand -base64 32

Config.Name: Stable node ID
Config.Description: Must stay STABLE across restarts. The application default is the container hostname, which Unraid regenerates whenever the container is recreated - the new container then counts as a new node and has to wait out the previous identity's session lease before re-adopting sessions.

Config.Name: Log level
Config.Description: error, warn, info or debug.

Config.Name: Enable Swagger API docs
Config.Description: Serves interactive API docs at /api/docs. OFF by default under NODE_ENV=production, and deliberately so: the docs mount is NOT behind the API-key guard, so anyone who can reach the port sees the full schema and the exact running version. Set true only on a trusted LAN.

Config.Name: Database type
Config.Description: sqlite (zero-config, stored in the appdata folder) or postgres. Switching to postgres additionally requires DATABASE_HOST, DATABASE_PORT, DATABASE_NAME, DATABASE_USERNAME and DATABASE_PASSWORD - add them as extra variables.

Config.Name: Database auto-sync schema
Config.Description: LEAVE false. With false, OpenWA applies its versioned migrations at boot - the correct path for an install you will upgrade over time. The first migration is a guarded baseline that creates the whole schema, so a brand-new database works fine. Setting true lets TypeORM reshape tables from the entity definitions instead, which can drop columns.

Config.Name: Storage backend
Config.Description: local (filesystem, inside the appdata folder) or s3 for an S3/MinIO backup and migration target.

Config.Name: Media path
Config.Description: Container-internal path for locally stored media. Keep it under /app/data so it lands in your mapped folder.

Config.Name: Session data path
Config.Description: Container-internal path for WhatsApp session auth and Chromium profiles. Keep it under /app/data or your linked sessions will not survive a container recreate.

Config.Name: Plugins directory
Config.Description: Where installed plugins land. Must be on the writable appdata mapping - the container root filesystem is read-only.

Config.Name: Chromium headless
Config.Description: Keep true. Only relevant to the whatsapp-web.js engine.

Config.Name: Chromium launch args
Config.Description: Comma-separated Chromium flags for the whatsapp-web.js engine. The defaults are what a container without a Chromium sandbox and without a large /dev/shm needs; do not remove them unless you know why.

Config.Name: whatsapp-web.js auth timeout (ms)
Config.Description: Optional. Raises the first-boot initialisation wait (default 30000). Increase to 60000-120000 if the QR code times out before WhatsApp Web finishes loading on a busy or low-powered server.

Config.Name: Trusted proxies
Config.Description: Optional. Set when running behind SWAG / Nginx Proxy Manager so rate limiting and audit logs see the real client IP instead of the proxy's, for example 172.18.0.0/16.

Config.Name: Public base URL
Config.Description: Optional. The externally reachable URL of this instance, for example https://openwa.example.com - used when building absolute links.

Config.Name: NODE_ENV
Config.Description: Do not change. production enables the security defaults and the production boot checks.

Config.Name: PORT
Config.Description: Container-internal listen port. Do not change - remap the host side on the WebUI port entry instead.

Config.Name: HOME
Config.Description: Do not change. The container root filesystem is read-only, so HOME must point at the writable tmpfs.

Config.Name: XDG_CONFIG_HOME
Config.Description: Do not change. Chromium resolves its home from the passwd entry and ignores HOME; without a writable config dir on the tmpfs it hard-crashes at launch on the read-only root filesystem.

Config.Name: XDG_CACHE_HOME
Config.Description: Do not change. See XDG_CONFIG_HOME.
